newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD injunction doesn't worry investors.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD injunction doesn't worry investors.

text.p: A Brazilian high court injunction suspending a federal land transfer to state mining giant CVRD does not worry investors planning to bid in the privatization auction of CVRD.
"We are not concerned," said Francisco Padilha, spokesman for Brazilian steelmaker CSN, which is leading one of two consortia taking part in the auction.
"We are going ahead. The formation of our consortium did not stop for one moment due to the court action."
There was no one available to comment on behalf of the other consortium, led by Brazilian metal, cement and pulp Votorantim and South Africa's Anglo-American Corp.

The injunction granted by a Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) Justice on Tuesday suspends the government's transfer of the right of use to CVRD of 411,000 hectares of land in the Carajas mining region in the northern state of Para.

Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), which oversees the privatization process, has said the court ruling does not affect CVRD's mining and exploration rights in the area and therefore does not warrant the delay of the auction.
The government has appealed the injunction and a full session of the STF's 11 members is due to rule today.

Analysts did not believe the consortia would be discouraged from participating in the April 29 auction of a 40-45-percent voting stake in CVRD because of the injunction, but they would seek further clarification on its implications.

Earlier Wednesday, the STF threw out a constitutional challenge to the privatization of CVRD, which sought an injunction against the April 29 sell-off. ((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
